messages:
Aisha Khan: Heads-up — BankSys (security team) wants a closed-DC POC. Their blockers: no outbound, no jumpbox, must accept customer root CA rotations, HSM for key material, and prefer delta updates delivered via USB/sneakernet. They also want model version pinning and an offline activation flow. Can we do this?

Tim Park: Quick clarifying Qs — do they require delta-only payloads (patches) or can we provide full signed images if needed? Also, any absolute NO for remote support (like remote-debug sessions)?

Aisha Khan: They said: "no outbound at all, ops will only accept signed artifacts delivered to a transfer station and then manually loaded. Remote debug is disallowed unless we ship engineers."

Maya Li: We can support this. Notes: 1) We already support customer CA truststores for Private deployments — we can import their root CA into the node truststore. 2) For offline cert rotation there's a detached-runbook pattern: operator generates CSR on the node, they sign it offline with their CA, then re-upload the cert artifact to the node. We'll need a runbook for each step. 3) HSM: we support PKCS#11 integrations for key storage; model artifact decryption keywrap will need a key-management adapter configured to their HSM (vendor-specific).

Tim Park: Packaging proposal (initial POC): deliver a signed full bundle + delta patch capability. Artifacts: OCI-style tar + detached signature + sbom. Example verification steps to include in runbook:

```
sha256sum redwood-bundle-1.2.0.tar.gz
gpg --verify redwood-bundle-1.2.0.tar.gz.sig redwood-bundle-1.2.0.tar.gz
cat redwood-bundle-1.2.0.sbom.json | jq '.components[] | {name,version}'
```

Also include an activation token binding step so the artifact can only be activated on the intended cluster (offline gating).

ops-bot: Release artifact note: 2025-02-04T12:03Z bundle v1.2.0-detached signed, sbom attached, checksum: sha256:fa3b9c... (artifact ID rwd-20250204-12).

Aisha Khan: Commercial question — can we commit to a 6-month upgrade cadence in the SOW, with emergency patches in-between? Customer expects predictable patches and occasional major upgrades. Pricing impact?

Tim Park: We typically treat major upgrades as opt-in for Private customers. For emergency CVE patches we offer an SLA (72h) on enterprise support; enforced 6-month upgrades would require a support uplift and possibly a managed-service addendum. I'll flag Commercial for pricing.

Maya Li: Rough engineering estimate: initial offline validation + runbook + packaging automation ~ 3 eng-weeks. Setting up PKCS#11 + test harness for their HSM vendor ~ 2-4 eng-weeks depending on vendor quirks. Ongoing delta-signing automation ~ 1 eng-week per quarter. Documenting the CA rotation runbook (customer-signed flow) ~ 2-3 days.

Aisha Khan: Next actions: Tim -> draft POC runbook & packaging checklist by EOD tomorrow; Maya -> list PKCS#11 vendor compatibility matrix and a sample offline cert-rotation runbook; I'll loop in Legal/Commercial for SOW language and pricing. :thumbsup:

Tim Park: Will do. I'll include a short 'operator checklist' for the transfer-station workflow and a sample artifact verification snippet.

Maya Li: Also recommend a short dry-run where we simulate rotation and patch via USB in our staging env before field POC. Saves time.

Aisha Khan: Agreed. Thanks — closing for now, will update with runbook link when ready.
